Exercise: Ab Roller

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
pull

Difficulty Level:
intermediate

Movement Patterns:

- horizontal_pulling

Primary Muscles:

- abdominals

Secondary Muscles:

- shoulders

Equipment:

- other

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
moderate

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:
None

Contraindications:

- condition: Lower back pain, reason: May exacerbate existing conditions due to the strain on the lower back.
- condition: Shoulder injury, reason: High shoulder involvement may aggravate pre-existing injuries.

Exercise Variations:

- name: Single Arm Ab Roller, force: pull, level: advanced, mechanic: compound, primaryMuscles: ['abdominals'], secondaryMuscles: ['shoulders']

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Bicycle Crunches, equipment: bodyweight
- exercise_name: Reverse Hyperextension, equipment: cable machine

Instructions:

- Hold the Ab Roller with both hands and kneel on the floor.
- Now place the ab roller on the floor in front of you so that you are on all your hands and knees (as in a kneeling push up position). This will be your starting position.
- Slowly roll the ab roller straight forward, stretching your body into a straight position. Tip: Go down as far as you can without touching the floor with your body. Breathe in during this portion of the movement.
- After a pause at the stretched position, start pulling yourself back to the starting position as you breathe out. Tip: Go slowly and keep your abs tight at all times.
